newsitem.title: GERMANY: Most of German SPD wants Schroeder to face Kohl.
newsitem.headline: Most of German SPD wants Schroeder to face Kohl.

text.p: More than two thirds of the members of Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) want Lower Saxony premier Gerhard Schroeder to challenge Chancellor Helmut Kohl in general elections due next year, according to a magazine poll.

The poll for Der Spiegel magazine, released on Saturday ahead of publication on Monday, showed 69 percent of those questioned wanted Schroeder to be their candidate for chancellor while only 27 percent favoured party leader Oskar Lafontaine.
The SPD has said it will not decide on its candidate for chancellor until after Schroeder has stood for reelection as Lower Saxony premier in March next year.
Kohl has already announced he will stand at the head of his centre-right coalition.
Schroeder told the magazine the poll did not change the plan to wait until next year before deciding on a candidate.

Opinion polls consistently show Schroeder as the SPD candidate best-placed to unseat Kohl but until now it had been widely assumed that the pro-business premier was not popular among the left-leaning grassroots of his own party.
The next general election is scheduled to take place in a period between late September and October next year. Kohl's government has not yet announced the exact date.

The Spiegel survey, carried out among 1,400 party members by the Emnid research group, also revealed the leadership's plan to wait until next year before choosing its leading candidate for the elections was unpopular.

The survey found 35 percent wanted the candidate to be chosen as soon as possible, 34 percent wanted the decision taken at a party conference in December and 31 percent favoured waiting until March next year.
But Lafontaine said the leadership would stick to its plan. "We have chosen our plan after plenty of thought," he told the magazine. "There is no reason to deviate from it."
